recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If Patient Administration wants KML references removed from detailed definitions or notes, handle that as a separate source-changing tracker rather than FHIR-5420 cleanup.
issue_request: FHIR-5420 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for the DSTU1 Location resource. It asked to replace or clarify the existing altitude short text 'Altitude as expressed in KML'; the final resolution says to follow tracker FHIR-5418, which updated KML coordinate short wording to WGS84 datum for latitude, longitude, and altitude.
initial_application: The original application commit cd2313dbc0 explicitly covered trackers 5418, 5419, and 5420 and changed the Location spreadsheet short/display text from KML wording to WGS84 datum for the position coordinates. It did not remove the detailed KML compatibility definition text.
additional_context: Location is active in source/fhir.ini. Current source/location/structuredefinition-Location.xml carries 'Altitude with WGS84 datum' as the altitude short while retaining KML value-domain/interpretation wording in the definition and notes, which is consistent with the Jira comment that KML compatibility remains useful. Later commit c526692beb0 only corrected the note locator wording and preserved that split; no relevant Zulip or Confluence evidence was found.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Editing the definition or notes would exceed the tracker scope and could remove useful compatibility guidance without a later work-group decision.
